**Finding: Compliant** — no audit right against us to constrain.

The agreement contains no audit, inspection or usage-verification right running against Mortgage Logic.com. I confirmed this by keyword search (audit, inspect, verify, records, books, monitor, premises) and by full reads of the planner's candidate sections plus the license and confidentiality sections:

- **§ 5–6 (Compensation / Documentation and Disputes)** — fee provisions run in our favour: we get supporting documentation on request and a right to contest charges. No reciprocal TrueLink verification right.
- **§ 8 (Client Covenants)** — compliance, access-restriction and content warranties only; no inspection right.
- **§ 3(e)** — we hold real-time access to usage statistics and raw log files, so TrueLink has no need for a usage audit.

Two access-flavoured provisions were reviewed and are not audits: § 8(f) permits TrueLink to implement technical anti-spam measures on its own hosted environment, and § 9 requires us to give access solely so TrueLink can perform Y2K repairs at its own cost. Neither is a verification right, and neither grants remote access to our systems (the walk-away trigger).

Because no audit right binds the Customer, there is nothing to limit on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access — the current position is stronger than the playbook's preferred outcome, so I proposed no redline. Worth noting for negotiation discipline: if TrueLink later seeks to add a usage-verification or compliance-audit right, we should hold to the preferred parameters (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access) rather than accept an unqualified right.
